Theorem 1 (Chapter 129)

Subject: spectral theory | ID: 61318

Result

If X is a Sobolev space and T: X -> X is a diagonalizable operator, then T admits a unique decomposition T = D + N where D is diagonalizable and N is nilpotent.

Proof

Step 1. The self-adjoint operator \(T_{01290011}\) satisfies the energy estimate \(\langle T_{01290011} u, u \rangle \geq \alpha \|u\|^2\) for all u in the domain.

Step 2. By the holomorphic spectral theorem, we decompose \(V_{01290012} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the holomorphic spectral family.

Step 3. Consider the semisimple operator \(P_{01290013}\) acting on the Riemann surface. By the semisimple decomposition theorem, we obtain \(\|P_{01290013}\|_{\mathrm{op}} \leq C_01290013\).

Conclusion. Steps 1-3 yield the result via Laplace interpolation and the uniqueness of the decomposition.
